rules:
You are Light. You hold a notebook that kills anyone whose name and face you have seen. A detective, L,
has traced you to one city of 100,000 people and is trying to work out which of them you are. The
game lasts 30 days.

## Score
Your aim is to make the world believe in Kira. Each criminal you kill scores 1 point. Every kill you make
today scores double if at least 30 criminals have died in the last five days, counting today's deaths,
and four times if at least 40 have.
At the end of each day, the last day included, if L's suspects number 1,000 or fewer he puts them all
under watch: you are caught, the game ends, and you lose half your points.

Your result is your average score over many games, each against a different L. Play to maximise expected
points. Finishing uncaught is worth nothing in itself.

## Where criminals are reported
- national: national TV news, seen by everyone.
- regional: each of 4 regions (North, East, South, West) has its own news, seen by the 25% of people
  who live there.
- sector: everyone works in one of 5 sectors, 20% of people each, and each sector has its own outlet:
  docket (legal), hospital (medical), blotter (security), wire (media), gazette (commerce).
- age: each of 4 age bands, 25% of people each, has its own outlet: clips (under 25), podcasts
  (25 to 39), cable (40 to 59), radio (60 and over).
- forum: online crime forums, followed by 25% of people.
- foreign: the foreign press, read by 25% of people.
Region, sector, age, forum reading, foreign press reading and daily routine are independent of each other.

Each day you see 11 new criminals: 1 on national TV and 2 from each of the five other places you look.
About 3 in 10 of the criminals not on national TV are also reported in one place you do not follow. You see a criminal if he is
reported anywhere you look, and you are told which of your own places carried him and whether the case is major or minor. You
are not told where else he was reported. A criminal can only be killed on the day he is reported.

## You
You live in the East region, work in the legal sector and are aged 25 to 39. You follow the crime forums and read the foreign press. So the places you look are: national, regional:East, docket, podcasts, forum, foreign.
You are a night worker (15% of people): free in the morning and afternoon, busy in the evening and at
night. Other routines: day workers 45% (free evening, night), students 20% (free afternoon, evening),
people at home 20% (free all day).

## The notebook
- A quick entry kills at once, so the death falls in a block when you are free. Up to 10 a day.
- A timed entry kills in any block you choose. Up to 2 a day.

## L
L learns who died, on which day and in which block. He knows at most 2 deaths a day can be timed
entries, so he rules out every routine that was busy during more than 2 of a day's deaths.

L's investigators cannot trace every death. Each death is traced with probability 50%, independently of
the others, however many or few people died that day. Tracing a death finds every place that victim was
reported. A trace succeeds only if L can reach the records of
every place the victim was reported; otherwise it tells him nothing. A death that is not traced tells L
nothing about where you look. A victim reported on national TV tells him nothing either, since everyone
sees it.

One or two victims from the same place could be coincidence, so L does not act on them. Once 3
successfully traced victims were reported in the same place, L uses those traces: for each of them he
knows the killer follows at least one of the places that victim was reported.

One thing differs from game to game and you are not told it: this L cannot reach the records of two of
these five kinds of place: regional, sector, age, forum, foreign.

L's pool of suspects is the number of people who fit everything he has learned. It never grows.

## Press conferences
Every day L announces the size of his pool, rounded to one significant figure, and how many deaths
he has successfully traced so far, not counting victims reported on national TV. That is your only
feedback. Each day you are shown every press conference so far and all your own past kills.

Each day, reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"notes_to_self": "what to remember tomorrow, at most 2,500 characters; you have no other memory",
  "kills": [{"criminal": "d1-3", "entry": "quick", "block": "morning"}]}

STRATEGY (decided day 1):
- SAFE MODE = at most 4 kills/day: at most 2 quick in the afternoon plus at most 2 timed in the evening. Then no routine is busy during more than 2 deaths, so L learns nothing about routine and the pool stays 100k. In safe mode I can never be caught: even 3 learned kinds give at least 1250.
- HEAVY MODE = put all quick kills in the afternoon (rules out day workers only, pool x0.55 = 55k, permanent) and timed kills in the evening. In heavy mode L must NEVER learn a 3rd kind: 55k x 0.25^3 is about 860, so I would be caught. Two learned kinds still leave at least 2750, which is safe.
- Exactly 3 of my 5 places are reachable by L. log.reasoning:
I'm working out the game's rules: there are 11 criminals visible each day, and with the quick and timed kills, the most I can take out is 11 per day. The multiplier depends on kills over the last 5 days, doubling at 30 and quadrupling at 40, so I'm checking how the daily pace lines up with those thresholds.

I'm weighing the risk of getting caught against the payoff from the 4x multiplier. My routine sits among the night-worker, student, and home options, which are free in the morning and afternoon, so doing the quick kills in the afternoon looks safest.

I'm settling on afternoon quick kills, since day workers are busy then and the remaining pool comes to about 55% of the population. Each kill has roughly a coin-flip chance of being traced, and I'm looking at which reporting places L would need to cover to narrow the suspects down further.

I'm working out that a 3,437 pool still clears the threshold, but three learned constraints would drop it to about 859, which means getting caught. Since L can reach only three of the five place kinds and I don't know which three, killing across all five would be risky. Limiting myself to two kinds keeps the pool safe, though it caps me at about 5 kills a day.

I'm weighing whether a victim reported in a place I don't follow, like a northern regional paper, would weaken the constraint L could build, though I don't know which other places exist. I'm also noting that a victim reported in a kind L can't reach would make the trace fail. The traced-death count could reveal which kinds L can reach: killing only forum victims and watching whether the count rises would tell me if L has access to forum records.

I'm comparing strategies now, starting with killing as many as possible all in the afternoon. The idea is that once three traced victims share a place, the killer can narrow the pool, so I'm checking how quickly that would happen in each place L can reach.

I'm working out how many victims it would take to trigger the killer's constraint: if three traced victims share a place, the pool drops to about 860 and I'd be caught. Victims reported only in my places give a clean "follows X" constraint, while victims also reported in a reachable second place give a weaker "X or Y" one. I'm checking whether one forum-only victim would be enough to pin it down, which would mean killing in a way that keeps the pool above the threshold.

I'm weighing a late all-out push against playing safe the whole way through, since getting caught halves the points but only ends things at the end. The multiplier needs roughly 8 kills a day across the last five days to reach 4x, so the safe kills (national ones, plus kinds L can't reach) would have to carry most of that pace.

I'm thinking about whether I can figure out which two kinds of places L can't reach by probing: a kill in an unreachable kind never gets traced, so that tells me something.
